title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from pp. 26-28: M is a poset (≤) with a second relation ≪ ("lies in the closure / shadow of"), assumed transitive. L ⊂ M is the set of 'points'. For X ∈ M, omb(X) = {x ∈ L | x ≪ X} is the closure ('ombre'). X~ = {Y ∈ M | Y ≤ X} are the strata or faces of X. Z \mathring{\ll} X means Z ≪ X and X is minimal among the Y ≤ X with Z ≪ Y. In particular omb(X)° = {x | x \mathring{\ll} X} is the 'open part' of X.

Axioms used:
- ML1 (relating points to faces).
- ML2: every omb(X)° is nonempty.
- ML3: the omb(Y)°, for Y ≤ X, cover omb(X). By the corollary on p. 26 they in fact partition it, so for x ≪ X there is a unique smallest Y ≤ X with x ≪ Y.

Aim of the page: derive the axiom At_M 4a), i.e. for all Z ≪ X there exists X' ≤ X with Z \mathring{\ll} X'. Here Z is an arbitrary element, not just a point, and the derivation goes from point-level axioms. This is a 'frontier condition' statement: the closure of a stratum is a union of strata, and every element of the closure of X lies in a unique minimal face.

Lemma 2. Let Z ≪ X, X' ≤ X and x ∈ L with x ≪ Z and x ≪ X'. If x \mathring{\ll} Z, then Z ≪ X', and x \mathring{\ll} X' ⇔ Z \mathring{\ll} X'.

Proof.
1. Grothendieck assumes a strengthened ML1, which the previous page hoped to deduce: there is Z' ≤ Z with Z' ≪ X' and x ≪ Z'.
2. Since x \mathring{\ll} Z, Z is minimal below Z with x ≪ Z, so Z' = Z and hence Z ≪ X'.
3. (⇒) If x \mathring{\ll} X' and Z ≪ X'' ≤ X', then x ≪ X'' by transitivity, so X'' = X'. Hence Z \mathring{\ll} X'.
4. (⇐) If Z \mathring{\ll} X', take X'' with x ≪ X'' ≤ X'. Then X'' ≤ X, so the first part, applied to X'', gives Z ≪ X''. Minimality of X' for Z forces X'' = X'. Hence x \mathring{\ll} X'.

Consequence. Given Z ≪ X, choose x \mathring{\ll} Z (ML2). Since x ≪ X, ML3 gives the unique X' ≤ X with x \mathring{\ll} X'. Lemma 2 then gives Z \mathring{\ll} X'. This is At_M 4a), obtained from strengthened ML1 plus ML2 and ML3.

The next page turns this into Corollaries 1-3. These characterise Z \mathring{\ll} X' by inclusion or intersection of open shadows, and by X' being the smallest element of X~^Z.
errors: Gap acknowledged by Grothendieck himself: the 'generalized ML1' (with an arbitrary Z in place of a point x) is simply assumed ('On admettra ML 1 sous forme généralisée'), though p. 26 had hoped to derive it from ML2/ML3. The reduction to point-level axioms is therefore only partial.
The step called 'tautologique' silently uses transitivity of ≪ (x ≪ Z ≪ X'' ⇒ x ≪ X''). This is presumably among the standing axioms but is not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Axiomatics of a 'stratified' combinatorial structure: elements with closures (omb) and open parts (omb°), faces Y ≤ X whose open parts partition the closure, and points as minimal elements
ideas.modern_name: Face posets of stratified spaces / frontier condition / closure-finite (regular) cell structures; posets with a closure relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (stratifications); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries et al.); combinatorial face posets (Björner and others)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme is announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6, but this axiomatics is unpublished as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Lemma 2: for x in the open part of Z, x is open in a face X' iff Z is open in X' (transfer of the minimal-face property from points to elements)
ideas.modern_name: Uniqueness of the carrier stratum / 'minimal face containing a cell' in a stratified poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore for CW and simplicial complexes (carrier of a point)

ideas.what: Deriving the element-level axiom At_M 4a) (every Z ≪ X has a unique minimal face X' ≤ X containing it) from point-level axioms ML1-3
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition deduced from pointwise partition of closures

missed.claim: Grothendieck wants to show that a 'point-based' axiomatics (ML1-ML3 on the subset L of minimal elements) implies the 'element-based' axiom At_M 4a). He only succeeds by assuming a strengthened ML1; whether plain ML1-ML3 suffice is left open.
missed.quote: On admettra ML 1 sous forme généralisée, pour conclure ici que ∃ Z' ≤ Z, Z' ≪ X' et x ≪ Z'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small piece of an unpublished combinatorial foundation for tame topology / stratified spaces. Its interest is mainly historical, as part of the 'Analysis situs' project; mathematically the statements are elementary poset combinatorics.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary order-theoretic lemma in an unpublished axiomatisation of stratified 'tame' spaces. It is historically interesting as a glimpse of the 1986 Analysis situs drafting, but the mathematics is routine (carrier-stratum properties), and the key step is assumed rather than proved.
transcription_corrections: Final reference should read 'At_M 4 a)' (subscript M, as on p. 26), not 'At_n'.
First line likely reads 'Donc on va démontrer [?] ...' or similar; 'parvenu' is doubtful. The line is illegible scribble and should be marked uncertain.

Line 'il en suit [?] par ce qui précède' is better read as '(... par ce qui précède, appliqué à X'' : X'' ≤ X) on a Z ≪ X'' ≤ X', et comme (on sait X' ≤ X) on a Z \mathring{\ll} X' ... on conclut X'' = X''.
